# Settlers of Colossus
A board game for one to four players about claiming the Colossus sector: run lanes between the stars, raise outposts and colonies, and trade your way to ten points. The boxed board is sold at the Wolfgate vendor.
## Sitting down Use the box in hand, on a table, or through its [bold]Play[/bold] verb to open the board. Take a seat and anyone seated can start the game; everyone else in reach can watch. Examining the box shows whether a game is being played on it.
Closing the window or walking away gives up your seat, but your pieces and cards stay in the game. Anyone can sit in a vacant seat and carry it on. While a seat is vacant its turns pass and anything it owes is played at random, and if every player leaves, the game waits for them.
## The board Nineteen sectors, each with a number from 2 to 12. When that number is rolled, every outpost on a corner of the sector earns one card and every colony two. - [bold]Salvage yard[/bold]: scrap - [bold]Ice field[/bold]: ice - [bold]Gas giant[/bold]: gas - [bold]Farm world[/bold]: biomass - [bold]Ore belt[/bold]: ore - [bold]Dead zone[/bold]: nothing; the pirates start here.
The dots under a number show how often it comes up. A 6 or an 8, in red, comes up the most.
## Setting up Each player places an outpost and a lane next to it, in turn order, and then a second pair in reverse order. The second outpost pays one card for each sector around it. Outposts can never sit on neighbouring corners.
## A turn Roll the dice; every sector with that number pays out. Then build, trade and play a contract in any order, and end your turn. - [bold]Lane[/bold] (scrap, ice): along a side joined to your lanes or buildings. - [bold]Outpost[/bold] (scrap, ice, gas, biomass): one point, on a corner your lanes reach. - [bold]Colony[/bold] (two biomass, three ore): upgrades an outpost to two points and doubles its income. - [bold]Contract[/bold] (gas, biomass, ore): a card drawn from the deck.
Lit corners and sides on the board show where you can build.
## Pirates A 7 pays nobody. Anyone holding more than seven cards discards half of them, then the roller moves the pirates to another sector and robs a player with a building beside it. The sector under the pirates earns nothing until they move on.
## Contracts You can play one contract a turn, before or after rolling, but not on the turn you bought it. - [bold]Escort[/bold]: move the pirates and rob, as on a 7. - [bold]Charter[/bold]: a hidden point. - [bold]Survey[/bold]: lay two lanes for free. - [bold]Windfall[/bold]: take any two resources from the bank. - [bold]Embargo[/bold]: name a resource; every other player hands you all of theirs.
## Trading On your turn, trade four of one resource to the bank for one of another. A dock on your outpost or colony makes it better: [bold]3:1[/bold] docks take any resource, [bold]2:1[/bold] docks only the one they show.
Any player can post an offer to the table, and any player who can pay it can accept. A trade always includes the player whose turn it is.
## Points and winning The first player to reach ten points on their own turn wins. Points come from: - [bold]Outposts[/bold]: one point each. - [bold]Colonies[/bold]: two points each, in place of the outpost they replaced. - [bold]Charters[/bold]: one point each. They stay hidden in your hand, so the others can't see them coming. - [bold]Longest route[/bold]: two points for the first player with five or more lanes in an unbroken line. It passes to anyone who builds a longer one. - [bold]Largest fleet[/bold]: two points for the first player to play three escorts. It passes to anyone who plays more.
The two setup outposts give everyone two points to start with. You have five outposts, four colonies and fifteen lanes to build with, so upgrading outposts to colonies frees them to be built again.
